name: Coder
one_liner: A self-hosted platform that moves development environments off laptops onto your own infrastructure, started on demand.

text.why: Every new hire loses days setting up a development environment. Coder defines that environment in Terraform and starts it on demand; idle workspaces shut down automatically to save cost, and access runs through a secure tunnel.
text.take: Too heavy for one person; the return shows up with a team — particularly one worried about where AI coding tools keep their keys.
build: Go under AGPL-3.0. Workspaces are defined in Terraform across EC2 VMs, Kubernetes pods or Docker containers, connected over a WireGuard tunnel. Coder Agents runs AI coding agents in the control plane on your own infrastructure, with no API keys inside workspaces.

who.role: Teams with several developers, projects with rotating contractors, and organisations that cannot let code sit on personal laptops.

start.text: Follow the quickstart at coder.com on a test server first, and gauge how much of your current setup has to move into Terraform.

caveat: You run the servers yourself. Under AGPL-3.0 a modified service must publish its source, and some capabilities sit behind a paid Premium tier.

license.scope_text: Release source if you redistribute or host it as a service.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
